--- API/sbShare.md ---
Configuration
Helpers behind sharing pages to another SilverBullet space. See [[^Library/Std/Infrastructure/SilverBullet Share]] and [[API/share]].

A shared page is addressed by a URI of the form `<space url>/<page name>`, for example `https://example.com/notes/Shared/Page`. Reads and writes use the other space’s `.fs` API with a token obtained through the device flow, kept under the credential key `sb:<space url>` (see [[API/auth]]).

One `net.readURI:` / `net.writeURI:` service pair handles every space. Its `match` resolves the URI when it is dispatched, so it claims URIs of any space known at that moment (from `share.silverbullet.spaces` or a stored credential), including spaces configured after this page loaded. Its priority is above the generic `https:` reader.

--- Guide/Desktop Setup.md ---
Install and open a space | Protect and troubleshoot your space
Back up your local folder and test a restore into a separate folder. Sync can copy an unwanted edit or deletion to another device, so it does not replace a backup.

If another device is missing an edit, first check the Server sync status in the space’s settings and whether the Server is reachable. If the issue is inside the shared editor, start with [[Log]] and [[Troubleshooting]]. The browser cache reset instructions on that page apply to browser clients, not Desktop’s local files.

For shared configuration and libraries across Desktop spaces, see [[Meta Space]].

--- API/share.md ---
API | API > share.sharePage(name?)
Shares a page according to its `share.*` frontmatter, the same as the `Share: Page` command. Without a name it shares the current page. Returns `true` when something was shared, `false` when there was nothing to do, and `nil` when the user already knows the outcome (a conflict, or a cancelled “Which version?” dialog). Errors with `Not configured` when the page has no `share.uri`.

--- Share.md ---
Modes | Workflow
In your writable space, open the page you want to share and run the `Share: Page` (bound to `Cmd-p`/`Ctrl-p` by default) command. This will pop up a list of enabled “Share providers”. Pick one and follow the provider-specific onboarding steps. At the end, your page will be shared and the `share.*` frontmatter keys automatically set.

Subsequent shares can be done simply by running the `Share: Page` command again.

For the current page, these commands exist:
* ${widgets.commandButton "Share: Open Remote"}: opens the shared copy in your browser, where the location has a web address.
* ${widgets.commandButton "Share: Copy Link"}: copies that web address.
* `Share: Unshare`: stops sharing the page, removing its `share.*` keys. The shared copy stays where it is.

--- API/share.md ---
API | API > share.unshare(name?)
Stops sharing a page: removes its `share.*` keys. The copy at the remote stays. Without a name it unshares the current page in the editor.
